what_happened.summary: Dropped third strike, runner on third, 1 out. Offense: First base is open, so the batter can run: sprint to first the moment the ball gets away. The runner on third watches the catcher: if the catcher throws to first, that's often the chance to break for home. Defense: Tag the batter if he's close, or throw to first. Before throwing, check the runner on third; the corner infielders should call it out. A rushed throw can give away the winning run. This applies only where your league uses the uncaught-third-strike rule. This guidance comes from draft coaching notes that haven't been reviewed yet.

output.call_type_rationale: The umpire's judgment decides what happened; a written rule then sets what follows.

channel.who: Your players, then the tournament director if a rule is unclear
channel.how: Talk to the team at the next practice; take any rule question to the director calmly between innings, never a judgment call.

output.teachable_moment: Big moments aren't scripted: The moments that matter most aren't planned. They happen because kids are put in situations where they can fail or succeed, and sometimes they succeed through what could have been failure.

individual: Two-strike rounds in batting practice: start every rep at 0-2, choke up, shorter swing, battle the outer half off a tee or soft toss.
Plan more short, active practices with stations rather than adding more games.
team: First-to-third reads: Runner at first on a ball in the outfield gap. Read the fielder’s angle and the cutoff, then decide stay-at-second vs. third without watching the ball bounce twice. Safety: No slides into unprotected coaches. Clear the rundown lane before the next rep.
at_home: Put kids in situations where they can fail or succeed. That's where growth and team belief come from.

life_lesson.text: You can't plan for every opportunity, but you can be ready for it and willing to take it.

lessons.title: Big moments aren't scripted
lessons.principle: The moments that matter most aren't planned. They happen because kids are put in situations where they can fail or succeed, and sometimes they succeed through what could have been failure.

situations.name: Dropped third strike, runner on third, 1 out
situations.offense: First base is open, so the batter can run: sprint to first the moment the ball gets away. The runner on third watches the catcher: if the catcher throws to first, that's often the chance to break for home.
situations.defense: Tag the batter if he's close, or throw to first. Before throwing, check the runner on third; the corner infielders should call it out. A rushed throw can give away the winning run.
situations.common_mistakes: Batter doesn't run because he thinks strike three ends it; runner on third doesn't read the throw; catcher throws to first without looking the runner back.
